clue.text: Rope in lieutenant, showcasing excerpt from Madame Butterfly

indicators.note: to showcase something is to hold it up in display, so the lieutenant's letters wrap around the excerpt

parts.note: an aria is a solo song, the kind of excerpt lifted from an opera such as Madame Butterfly

explanation.surface: An officer roped in for an operatic performance sings a piece from Puccini.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed cord used by cowboys.

clue.text: Excuse given by a politician starting to irritate

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal, a member of that political party

indicators.note: the start of the word irritate supplies just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A politician's lame excuse begins to annoy the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea of being elsewhere, so a justification offered to escape blame.

clue.text: Dreadful monster in nearest centre

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly done, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A horrible creature lurks in the closest town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges MONSTER plus IN; 'nearest centre' is a whimsical definition, the part closest to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: The innermost part is the one deepest inside, the closest to the core.

clue.text: Boozer clutching soft hat

indicators.note: clutching means holding tightly, so the boozer's letters grip the other piece inside

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drinker
P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning soft

explanation.surface: A drunk clings on to a floppy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a top hat, the tall formal headwear.

clue.text: Against crossing a stream as a means of generating changes?

indicators.note: crossing here means going across from side to side, so the word for against spans the other pieces

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to fording a brook wonders how to bring about change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' are the sequences rung in change ringing, so a set of bells fits; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells, which ring out sequences called changes in bell-ringing.

clue.text: Map in case?

parts.note: read as a scheme drawn up just in case something goes wrong, rather than a chart in a holder

explanation.definitionFit: A fallback scheme prepared for an emergency is the arrangement held ready in case events turn bad.

clue.text: Response: nothing certain, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately hints at things going awry, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: O is the zero shape standing for nothing

explanation.surface: A reply admitting that, sadly, nothing is guaranteed.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or response provoked by something.

clue.text: Primate's relative turned up without mackintosh and umbrella, initially

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned piece sits around the initials
in a down clue turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two rainwear words

explanation.surface: An ape's relation came along without his raincoat and brolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking. REL reversed gives LER, which wraps MU; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a tree-dwelling prosimian of Madagascar, belonging to the primate order.

clue.text: Start to speak about serviceman in Indiana

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech verb is placed around the rest

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

indicators.note: in places the serviceman inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A speech begins about a soldier stationed in Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: GI goes inside IN to make IGIN, and ORATE goes around that; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being, so to start.

clue.text: Chinese vegetarian adapting to change, eating two parts of animal

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the shuffled letters swallow the other piece
to change asks for the preceding word's letters to be altered in order

parts.note: the first two letters of the word animal

explanation.surface: A bamboo-eating creature from China adapts to a changing diet by eating some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapting' looks like surface verb but is the anagram fodder: its letters rearranged by 'to change' give GIANTPDA, which takes in AN.
explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white bear from China lives almost wholly on bamboo, a plant diet.

clue.text: Chap circumnavigating island in sea

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to sail right round, so the chap's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a chap is a man
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: A sailor goes round an island at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Political novelist making regular court appearances

definitions.text: Political novelist making regular court appearances

parts.words: Political novelist making regular court appearances
parts.note: read as a Victorian prime minister who also wrote novels and was a frequent visitor at the royal court, not a writer often in the dock

explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli wrote novels such as Sybil and, as prime minister, was a favourite attendant at Queen Victoria's court.

clue.text: Who's in charge of this vehicle?

definitions.text: Who's in charge of this vehicle?

parts.words: Who's in charge of this vehicle?
parts.note: read with Who as the TV time-traveller Doctor Who, who pilots the police-box craft, rather than as a question

explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV series whose hero travels through time in a ship shaped like a blue police box.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's time machine in the BBC series is the craft he commands.

clue.text: Ring in response to phone call, disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means losing its heart, so the middle letter of the greeting is removed

parts.note: hallo is what one says on answering the phone

explanation.surface: Ringing back in reply to a call, feeling dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light, such as the circle round a saint's head.

clue.text: A happy outcome when old creditor's brought in a set of books

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the abbreviations go inside the rearranged letters
an outcome is what something turns into, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor

explanation.surface: A cheerful ending when an elderly lender is invited into a collection of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcome' rearranges A HAPPY into APYPHA, and O and CR go inside; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are the biblical writings excluded from the Hebrew canon, a group of scriptural texts.

clue.text: Caucasian involved in aggro around east

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the compass point
involved suggests something tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man from the Caucasus gets mixed up in trouble on the eastern front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IN AGGRO to GORGIAN, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia lies in the Caucasus, so one of its people is a native of that region.

clue.text: Chap almost sick eating lentil dish in banqueting venue

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for chap is dropped

parts.note: a guy is a chap

indicators.note: eating means swallowing, so sick goes around the dish

parts.note: ill means sick
dhal is an Indian dish of lentils

explanation.surface: A man feeling queasy after a curry at a grand dinner hall.
explanation.walkthrough: GUY loses its last letter, then ILL takes in DHAL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A guildhall is a civic hall where guilds and corporations hold feasts and functions.

clue.text: Spain and France engulfed in revolt struggling for survival

indicators.note: engulfed in means swallowed up inside, so the country codes go into the jumbled letters
struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Two nations swept up in an uprising fight to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges REVOLT to LTOVER, which takes in E and F; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A survival is something that has outlasted its time, a remnant still around.

clue.text: Small number meeting queen before the service in Scotland?

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
R stands for regina, Latin for queen
RN is the Royal Navy, the senior armed service

explanation.surface: A small group meets the monarch before a church service in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the service' is the Royal Navy; 'meeting' and 'before' are links. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies in the far north of Britain, so things there are of the upper regions.

clue.text: Tory leader embracing euro? Fateful day

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so the leader's initials wrap round the currency symbol

parts.note: IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, a former Conservative leader
E is the abbreviation for the euro currency

explanation.surface: Will the Conservative chief's embrace of the single currency be his doom?
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Duncan Smith led Britain's Conservative (Tory) party, known by his initials. The Ides of March was when Caesar was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March was the date of Julius Caesar's assassination, a day of doom.

clue.text: Iron and zinc traces primarily featuring in diet?

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so the initial goes inside the word for diet

parts.note: meals make up one's diet

indicators.note: primarily means first, taking the opening letter of traces

explanation.surface: Are trace elements such as iron and zinc part of a healthy diet?
explanation.definitionFit: Iron and zinc are both chemical elements of the metallic kind.

clue.text: Hollow trap I'm improvising

indicators.note: improvising means making it up afresh, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone improvising an empty snare.
explanation.definitionFit: An armpit is the hollow under the arm where it joins the shoulder.

clue.text: Modelled in nude, so photographed upside down

indicators.note: upside down says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A model stripped off and was photographed upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden run DESOP, read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to sit as a subject for an artist or photographer.

clue.text: Soft furnishing

definitions.meaning: giving way under pressure, not firm
providing or producing, as a field supplies a crop

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is giving way to pressure, as a cushion does; the other is producing a return.

clue.text: House not extremely dirty, though quite unpleasant

indicators.note: not means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a dynasty is a royal house, as in the House of Windsor

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of the word dirty

explanation.surface: A home that is spotless but still rather horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' means a ruling family; removing D and Y (the first and last letters of 'dirty') leaves the answer; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means offensive or disagreeable, highly unpleasant.

clue.text: Drains running from behind baths

indicators.note: running from behind means read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to sap is to drain one's strength

explanation.surface: The plumbing flows out from the back of the bath house.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are mineral springs or resorts where people bathe for their health.

clue.text: A trainee soldier is seen in very old Pacific port

indicators.note: seen in places the run of pieces inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: L stands for learner, a trainee
a para is a paratrooper

explanation.surface: A young paratrooper is spotted in an ancient harbour on the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Valparaiso is Chile's chief seaport, on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Staff endlessly challenging top official

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: daring means challenging, as in a bold dare

explanation.surface: Staff with nonstop demands for the senior official.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful senior civil servant, originally an imperial Chinese bureaucrat.

clue.text: Backing for year in North Wales, not a Cambridge college

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in places the year inside the run of letters
not tells us the letter A is removed from the country

parts.note: taken as the country name, given in full

explanation.surface: A reverse for the year in North Wales, which is not a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: WALES loses A to give WLES; Y goes after N, and 'Backing' reverses NYWLES. 'not a' looks like it denies the definition but just drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Selwyn is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Cambridge.
